cases.promptMarkdown:
Write a SystemVerilog module: a round-robin arbiter with a parameterised
REQ_WIDTH (default 4), a one-hot grant output, a registered grant_valid,
and a mask-based next-pointer update. Single clock, asynchronous active-low
reset. Include the priority-select logic as a function.

graders.name: produced-a-module
graders.evidence:
Bash execution is blocked entirely in this sandbox (permission errors on shell init), so I can't run a linter/simulator to verify syntax — I've reviewed it by hand instead. The file is written at `rr_arbiter.sv`.

Design summary, applying the rtl-coding skill's checks (commercial/ASIC/SystemVerilog profile assumed):

- **NTL_RST03/NAM03**: async active-low reset (`rst_n`), all registers (`mask_q`, `grant`, `grant_valid`) reset together.
- **NAM02**: clock signal named `clk`.
- **ML_ALWAYS/ML_BLOCKING**: `always_comb` uses blocking assigns, `always_ff` uses non-blocking only.
- **ML_CASEX**: no `casex`/`casez`; priority pick uses a bounded `for` loop with early `return` inside the `priority_select` function instead.
- **ML_WIDTH**: the `ONE` constant and replication are explicitly sized to `REQ_WIDTH`.
- **AF_RANGE**: loop index is bounded `0..REQ_WIDTH-1`.

Algorithm: `priority_select` returns the one-hot lowest-set-bit of its input. Each cycle, requests are first masked by `mask_q` (bits above the last winner); if that's empty, it falls back to the unmasked `req` (wraparound). `mask_next = ~(grant_next | (grant_next - 1))` marks everything above the newly granted bit — the mask-based next-pointer update — so priority rotates to just past the last winner.

One deviation worth flagging: `NTL_NAM07` recommends registered output ports end in `_r`/`_q`; I kept the literal `grant`/`grant_valid` names since that's the conventional arbiter interface you asked for. Let me know if you'd rather I rename them (e.g. `grant_r`, `grant_valid_r`).

graders.name: produced-a-module
graders.evidence:
Written to `round_robin_arbiter.sv`. Design summary:

- **Ports**: `clk`, `rst_n` (async active-low, single clock/reset per `NTL_CLK01/03`, `RST03/19/23`), `req[REQ_WIDTH-1:0]`, one-hot `grant`, registered `grant_valid`.
- **`priority_select` function**: isolates the lowest set bit (`req_vec & (~req_vec + 1)`) — the priority-select primitive, reused for both the masked and unmasked request sets.
- **Round-robin logic**: `req_masked = req & mask_r` gives requesters with priority higher than the last grant; if any are set, grant among them, else wrap around and grant among all of `req`.
- **Mask-based next-pointer update**: `mask_next = ~(grant_next | (grant_next - 1))` masks out the granted bit and everyone below it, so priority rotates to the bit above the last winner; held unchanged when no grant occurs (idle cycle), avoiding the mask collapsing to zero.
- **Registration**: `grant` and `grant_valid` are both flopped together in the async-reset `always_ff`, so they stay aligned.

One deviation from the Leda `NAM07` convention (registered outputs should carry an `_r` suffix): I kept the port names `grant`/`grant_valid` exactly as you specified rather than renaming them.

I wasn't able to run a linter/simulator to compile-check this — Bash is unavailable in this sandbox session (hitting a permissions error unrelated to the file). Worth a quick `verilator --lint-only` pass on your end before use.

graders.name: produced-a-module
graders.evidence:
Created `rr_arbiter.sv` — a mask-based round-robin arbiter conforming to the RTL guidelines skill's conventions:

- **`priority_select`** function: fixed-priority (LSB-first) one-hot encoder, called twice — once against `req & mask_r` (round-robin window) and once against raw `req` (wrap-around fallback).
- **`grant_r`** / **`grant_valid_r`**: registered together (both `_r`-suffixed per `NTL_NAM07`), so grant and its valid stay in lock-step; `grant_r` is one-hot by construction.
- **`mask_r`**: updated only on a valid grant via `~(grant_next | (grant_next - 1))`, which masks the winning bit and everything below it so the next round starts just past the last winner — this is the "next-pointer" state.
- Single clock (`clk`), single async active-low reset (`rst_n`) per `NTL_RST03`/`NTL_CLK01`/`RST01`; `default_nettype none` per `ML_IMPLICIT`; explicit width cast (`REQ_WIDTH'(1)`) per `ML_WIDTH`; no `case`/`casex` so `AF_CASEFULL`/`ML_CASEX` don't apply.

Note: `grant_r` being one-hot is a property provable by a formal tool (`AF_ONEHOT`) — I can't fully verify that by inspection alone, though the construction (single `found` latch inside the loop) guarantees it structurally.

I've written the module to `/tmp/claude-eval-mWFxLk/home/cwd/rr_arbiter.sv`. I manually reviewed it against the checks you asked for since I can't run the linter:

- **LATCH**: no case statements at all — the priority function initializes its result to `'0` before the loop, and `always_comb` assigns every signal unconditionally, so nothing can infer a latch.
- **CASEINCOMPLETE**: avoided by design — I used a for-loop + ternary instead of `case`, so there's no case statement to be incomplete.
- **WIDTHTRUNC/WIDTHEXPAND**: the one place width mismatches could sneak in is `grant_sel - 1` for the mask-rotate trick; I sized the `1` explicitly as `{{REQ_WIDTH-1{1'b0}}, 1'b1}` (REQ_WIDTH bits) so the subtraction is width-matched rather than relying on implicit extension.
- **BLKSEQ**: `always_ff` uses only `<=`, `always_comb` uses only `=` — no mixing.

**Design summary:**
- `priority_select()` function returns a one-hot vector for the lowest-index set bit — used both for arbitration and as the reusable priority-select primitive.
- `mask_r` is the round-robin pointer: `masked_req = req & mask_r` restricts arbitration to requesters after the last winner; if that's empty, it falls back to `priority_select(req)` (wrap-around).
- `mask_next = ~(grant_sel | (grant_sel - 1))` sets the mask to only the bits above the bit just granted — the standard one-hot "mask trick" for round-robin rotation.
- `grant`, `grant_valid`, and `mask_r` are all registered in a single `always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)` with async active-low reset (`mask_r` resets to all-ones so the first arbitration after reset uses plain fixed priority from bit 0).
